sources.title: Law No. 29-2017: conditions for entry, stay and exit of foreigners
sources.publisher: Official Journal / General Secretariat of the Government of the Republic of the Congo
sources.officialityEvidence: The Republic of the Congo’s General Secretariat of Government hosts the Official Journal containing promulgated Law No. 29-2017, which governs foreigner entry, including visitors.
sources.supportingExcerpt: non ressortissant d’un pays ayant des accords particuliers ... un passeport avec visa en cours de validité

sources.title: CEMAC: Member States
sources.publisher: Economic and Monetary Community of Central Africa
sources.officialityEvidence: CEMAC’s official Commission website identifies the six current member States, allowing the five foreign Member-State ordinary-passport codes to be mapped for Congo.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Cameroun, le Congo, le Gabon, la Guinée Équatoriale, la République de Centrafrique et le Tchad.

sources.title: CEMAC Commission President interview on free movement
sources.publisher: Economic and Monetary Community of Central Africa
sources.officialityEvidence: The official CEMAC Commission site’s current account states that visa-free free movement for Member-State citizens is effective.
sources.supportingExcerpt: L’effectivité de la libre circulation des citoyens des pays membres de la CEMAC, sans visa, est une réalité indéniable.

sources.title: Common Convention on free movement and right of establishment
sources.publisher: Economic and Monetary Community of Central Africa
sources.officialityEvidence: CEMAC publishes the Common Convention in its official legal archive. Its free-movement provisions cover Union Member-State nationals travelling as tourists and specify the document and three-month conditions.
sources.supportingExcerpt: La libre circulation de ces personnes comporte le droit de se déplacer et de séjourner ... pendant une durée de 3 mois

policies.title: Foreign CEMAC ordinary passports: Republic of the Congo short-visitor visa exemption
policies.summary: CEMAC’s current Commission material confirms effective visa-free movement for its Member-State citizens. The five foreign CEMAC passports are mapped to visa-free admission to the Republic of the Congo. The published common convention describes a three-month tourist rule and document conditions, while the Republic of the Congo’s foreigner law otherwise preserves particular immigration agreements and does not establish a named residual route.
conditions: Applies to nationals holding ordinary passports of the five other current CEMAC Member States: Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Gabon and Equatorial Guinea.

The published CEMAC common convention describes tourist free movement for up to three months and requires the community traveller to produce a valid or recently expired national identity card or passport and an international health booklet. The current Commission interview confirms visa-free movement but does not independently restate the duration; verify the convention’s continuing implementation before relying on that limit.

It does not establish a right to work, long-term residence, transit, diplomatic, official, service, crew, refugee or other special-document treatment. Entry remains subject to the applicable border, health, public-order, security and admissibility controls.
No current source reviewed establishes that an eVisa project, an online service, or case-specific arrival facilitation is an alternative nationality-wide route for this policy.
